1.title: Strip white coating off wire ends
1.say: Hold the blue stripping tool in your right hand. Push one white wire tip in about one centimetre. Squeeze the tool and pull the loose coating off both wire ends.
placements: white wire on left side of blue mat → about one centimetre of white coating removed from tip to leave copper showing, cut with blue stripping tool closed around coating (in the video: left curve of loop)
white wire on right side of blue mat → about one centimetre of white coating removed from tip to leave copper showing, cut with same blue tool (in the video: right curve near bottom)
watch_for: if the copper strands look cut short or frayed, the tool was closed too far back or squeezed too hard
if no shiny copper shows, the cut white sleeve is still on, pull it fully off
1.check_yourself: It should look like two white wires lying apart with short copper tips showing.
1.safety: Keep your fingers clear of the jaws of the blue stripping tool.

2.title: Twist bare copper ends together
2.say: Lay the two white wires so the copper tips overlap. Push the copper tips together to hook them. Twist the hooked copper round and round with your fingertips to lock it.
placements: left white wire bare copper tip → overlapped and twisted around right wire copper tip at centre to make a small tight join (in the video: bottom centre of loop on blue mat)
right white wire bare copper tip → overlapped and twisted around left wire copper tip at same centre join (in the video: bottom centre of loop on blue mat)
watch_for: if the join pulls apart when you let go, you did not twist the copper enough to lock it
if white coating is caught inside the twist, push the wires less far together so only copper touches
2.check_yourself: It should look like one white wire loop with a small twisted copper join in the middle.

3.title: Dab cleaning liquid on copper join
3.say: Hold the white wire loop steady. Dab the wet cleaning liquid called flux onto the twisted copper join. Use the thin black stick to spread a little all over the copper.
placements: clear flux liquid → dabbed onto twisted copper join at centre of white wire loop with thin black stick until copper looks wet (in the video: bottom centre of loop)
thin black applicator stick → touched to copper join to coat it (in the video: held from top centre)
watch_for: if the copper still looks dry and dull, you put on too little liquid, add another dab
if clear liquid runs far onto the white coating, you used too much, wipe the extra away from the white
3.check_yourself: It should look like the twisted copper join looks wet and shiny in the middle of the white loop.
3.safety: Keep the wet cleaning liquid off your skin and out of your eyes, then wash your hands.

4.title: Melt solder over copper join
4.say: Melt a little silver solder onto the hot soldering iron tip first. Press the hot tip against the wet copper join. Touch the thin silver wire to the join in the white loop until silver spreads.
placements: hot soldering iron tip with a little melted silver on it → pressed against twisted copper join at centre of white wire loop to heat it (in the video: bottom centre of loop on blue mat)
thin silver solder wire → touched to the heated join from the side until melted silver flows through and round to cover it (in the video: fed from right side)
watch_for: if the silver balls up and will not spread, the join is not hot enough or needs more wet cleaning liquid
if the white coating melts back and shrinks, you held the hot tip on too long, lift sooner
4.check_yourself: It should look like the centre join is covered with shiny silver joining the white wires.
4.safety: Do not touch the hot tip or the fresh join, hold the white coating back.

5.title: Slide black tube over join
5.say: Push the short black tube onto one white wire end. Slide the black tube along to the centre silver join. Leave a little white coating showing past each end of the black tube.
placements: short black shrink tube → slid from open end of white wire along white wire to centre over silver join with white coating showing past each end (in the video: bottom centre of loop)
watch_for: if the tube will not slide over, the silver join is too spiky, let it cool and smooth it down first
if shiny silver still shows outside the tube, the tube is off centre, move it until white shows both sides
5.check_yourself: It should look like a black tube covers the silver join with white coating visible on both sides.

6.title: Heat tube till it grips tightly
6.say: Hold the white wire steady beside the black tube. Point the hot gun nozzle just above the black tube. Move the heat slowly along the tube until it shrinks tight.
placements: silver hot gun nozzle → held just above black tube at centre of white wire loop and moved slowly along tube until tube shrinks tight (in the video: metal nozzle from top over bottom centre)
black shrink tube → heated until tight and smooth around white wire over join (in the video: bottom centre of loop)
watch_for: if the black tube bubbles or the white coating melts, the nozzle is too close or held still too long, lift it higher and keep moving
if the tube is still loose and wrinkled, you took the heat away too soon, warm it a little longer
6.check_yourself: It should look like the black sleeve is tight and smooth around the white wire over the join.
6.safety: Do not touch the hot nozzle or the fresh tube, let it cool first.
